t: Maximize Total Tastiness of Purchased Fruits — 2D Knapsack
o: Classic knapsack with an extra coupon dimension: each fruit costs price[i] (or floor(price[i]/2) with a coupon), gives tastiness[i], buy at most once, budget maxAmount, at most maxCoupons coupons. n ≤ 100, amounts ≤ 1000, coupons ≤ 5 — a DP over (money used, coupons used) is tiny. Example 2: with 2 coupons, buy fruits 2 and 3 at half price (7 + 3 = 10) for tastiness 28. The state dp[a][c] = best tastiness spending ≤ a money and ≤ c coupons handles everything.
k: Two-resource knapsack: dimensions are remaining money and remaining coupons.
Half price is floor(price/2), applied per fruit at most once.
Iterate items outer, resources downward to reuse a 2D (or 3D) table safely.

a.i: dp[i][a][c] = max tastiness considering first i fruits with budget a and coupons c. Each fruit: skip, buy plain, or buy with coupon.
s: For each fruit, for each a from high to low, c from high to low: take max of skip, buy (a ≥ price), buy with coupon (c > 0, a ≥ price/2).

a.i: Since each fruit is processed once, iterating money and coupons downward lets a single 2D table dp[a][c] serve as 'best using items so far', cutting memory.
s: For each fruit, loop a downward then c downward; update dp[a][c] with buy and coupon-buy options.

w: Present the 3D formulation to show understanding, then optimize to rolling 2D. Pitfalls: half price is floor division (price 7 → 3), and iterating downward is essential so each fruit is used once. Note prices/tastiness can be 0. Follow-up: maximize tastiness with exactly maxCoupons used, or print the chosen fruits (keep parent pointers).
